headline: 69% of enterprises share API keys across AI agents
summary: Enterprises are vulnerable to security breaches due to shared API keys across AI agents.
details: A recent survey by VentureBeat found that 69% of enterprises share API keys across AI agents, making them vulnerable to security breaches. This practice allows a single compromised agent to inherit the reach of all agents using the same key.

caption:
Can a single API key bring down an entire enterprise? 69% of enterprises share API keys across AI agents.

A recent survey by VentureBeat found that 69% of enterprises share API keys across AI agents, making them vulnerable to security breaches. This practice allows a single compromised agent to inherit the reach of all agents using the same key.

The survey of 107 enterprises revealed that 54% have already had an agent security incident or near-incident. Only 32% of enterprises give every AI agent its own scoped, managed identity.

Major security companies such as Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Cisco have made significant acquisitions to address this issue. Palo Alto Networks acquired CyberArk for $21.1 billion, while CrowdStrike acquired SGNL for $740 million.

The survey also found that 49% of enterprises enforce scoped permissions at runtime, and 47% monitor and log agent activity. However, only 30% sandbox their highest-risk agents.

#AI #SECURITY #ENTERPRISE #TECH

Source: VentureBeat
